newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil studies gas link to Denmark.
newsitem.headline: Statoil studies gas link to Denmark.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS said on Thursday it planned to incorporate a T-piece into the Europipe II gas trunkline running from Kaarstoe near Stavanger to Emden in northern Germany to enable later hook-up of a spur line to Denmark.
The planned 28-inch spur will run for 120 km (75 miles) and carry Norwegian gas to a receiving station at Nybro on the west Jutland coast.
Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said the state-owned energy company was studying the scheme for Norway's Gas Negotiating Committee, which is in sales talks with Dansk Olie og Naturgas.
Statoil said the sales negotiations, which cover up to two billion cubic metres of gas per year starting in 1999, were expected to end this year and would determine whether the spur would go ahead.
The line would have sufficient capacity to accommodate possible gas for transit to Sweden via the existing Danish network, Statoil said.
